basics.name: Sandy (Alexandra) Tayts
basics.label: Senior Product and Service Designer
basics.summary: I take complex workflows from research to a shipped product: I talk to the people who do the work, decide with the team what to build, design it, and often build it myself with AI. I work well in teams of any size, but I shine in a small team inside a large, complex program, where I also organize the wider cross-functional process and its stakeholders. That is the kind of role I’m looking for, full-time or contract.

work.name: InkPromptu
work.summary: Design and consulting practice: Shopify and Salesforce consulting, custom work for private clients, and AI product design, including UX and UI for Loomik, an AI sales-coaching platform. Two selected projects below.
highlights: LAZY (founder, product designer and builder): took a website service for vacation-rental hosts from idea to production, owning the offer, pricing, product, brand, and launch.
LAZY: researched 15 host communities through 60 posts and 200+ responses, discovering that guest trust, rather than price, was the main barrier to direct bookings.
LAZY: prototyped an editor hosts can’t break before designing any page layouts, then built a token-based design system with seven layouts and one-click skins.
LAZY: shipped the product to production in four months using Claude Code and Codex, including a guest-facing AI assistant, and stress-tested it across 15 very different demo homes.
LAZY: created the brand, illustrated mascot, advertising, marketing site, and supporting design system.
LAZY: launched Pleasant Street, a directory of independently owned vacation homes booked directly, to build links and search authority for participating hosts.
LAZY: reached 10 live hosts within five weeks of launch.

Rancourt & Co. (Shopify consultant and service designer): redesigned and rebuilt the Shopify store for a heritage Maine shoemaker that made Team USA’s Olympic ceremony shoes and makes shoes for Saint Laurent, Ralph Lauren, Brooks Brothers, Cole Haan, and Sperry.
Rancourt: ran discovery workshops and six moderated user tests, and cut the main menu from nine items to five.
Rancourt: modeled products in Shopify metaobjects, reducing 14,000+ product patterns to 150 with a shared parts library.
Rancourt: built the store with Claude Code and set it up so the brand’s team manages it on their own.
Rancourt: fixed 11,525 broken URLs and 3,940 server errors, and cut third-party apps from 24 to 2.
Rancourt: raised mobile Lighthouse performance from 37 to 100 and accessibility from 85 to 100 while keeping search rankings.

work.name: Wipro Digital
work.position: Managing Consultant, Product Owner and Designer
work.summary: Worked hands-on on every engagement below and, as design lead for the practice’s North America branch, designed solutions for 60+ RFP responses, set design standards, ran design reviews, and hired designers.
highlights: BP sales modernization (UX and service designer, DocuSign delivery lead, 2021–2023): redesigned and standardized sales processes across four markets with $2.1B in annual sales, consolidating four processes into one with 25% fewer steps and delivering the largest US DocuSign CLM implementation as of 2023.
BP: established a design-first approach across the Salesforce, Automation, and DocuSign teams, owned and presented all design deliverables in nine time zones, and launched a Center of Excellence.
BP: consolidated 60,000 pages of market-specific contracts into a modular template architecture of under 1,000 pages before development began.
BP: as DocuSign delivery lead of a six-person team, defined the Salesforce-to-DocuSign contract lifecycle, with an OAuth 2 integration that eliminated up to 95% of duplicate data entry.
BP: cut deal cycle time from 15.5 to 8 days and manual processes from 35 to 8, and raised agreements stored digitally from 30% to 98% and positive user experience from 55% to 83%.

EY Digital Hub (UX and service designer, Wipro proposal team, 2019–2020): designed Digital Hub, the centerpiece of Wipro’s 2019 bid for EY: a proactive IT-support service that resolves issues before employees notice them.
EY: directed discovery with a seven-person team (stakeholder workshops, interviews, 30+ surveys, and incident analysis), and validated every journey against platform capabilities before design.
EY: aligned Wipro’s Automation, ServiceNow, and Genesys teams on one support model: self-service for requests, AI-bot resolution for issues, and human-handled tickets only for what remains.

EY: consolidated 3+ support channels into one app with real-time request status, addressing the six root causes behind 76% of tickets, and delivered a wireflow explorer (https://sandy.tayts.com/dh-map/wireflows.html) and a five-year roadmap.
EY: reached the final round, where the client rated Digital Hub the strongest part of the proposal; it became the basis of 50+ Wipro bids and the award-winning Connected Employee.
IT Automation (AI-assisted B2B SaaS): owned the roadmap and delivery of AI-assisted B2B SaaS, and defined the KPIs that achieved 30% ticket deflection for IT Automation.
Clients: BP, Humana, EY, Warner Bros., Estée Lauder.

work.name: CAFEX
work.summary: Designed the Angular front end and a design system for desktop CRM platforms. Defined customer journeys, process flows and specifications for an omnichannel Microsoft Dynamics CRM app. Won Microsoft approval on the first handoff and earned preferred-product status within four months of release.

work.name: Various Clients

Endurance International Group (web hosting): designed client dashboards for hosting customers.
Vecna (workforce-management software): led user research, roadmap, delivery planning, and prototyping.
Careport (medical web app): designed and built the front end of an ADA-compliant medical web app used across Massachusetts hospitals.

work.name: Adobe
work.summary: Led an 18-person vendor team for localized Flash (Animate), and proposed and shipped 20+ features. Set localization and terminology standards adopted across the Adobe suite.
